briefFidelity: FAIL, and the evidence is that I wrote the violation down before I was told it was forbidden. The brief says the market 'may register, but only faintly... nothing that a casual viewer would notice at thumbnail size. Do not manufacture drama.' Unprompted, at Stage 1, I wrote that at 120px 'the stress row is unmistakable... the scattered, edge-clipping frames read as broken from across the sheet.' 1203347 stress loses its outer circle entirely and becomes a tumbling drift of squares running out of the top-left corner; 1283437 stress inflates until it crosses the top and both side edges; 1243682 stress swaps its circle for a diamond and fans its crown to both margins; 1310661 stress shrinks and tilts inside a square that does not exist in its neutral. That is manufactured drama and it is the loudest thing on the sheet. The brief also declares what varies between tokens: 'the number of enclosures and the character of the centre.' That is not what varies. What varies is the container SHAPE (circles on 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1475115, 1561509, 1985692; hexagons on 1310661, 1366079, 1446330, 1733538; a square on 1835793; a diamond on 1991107) plus symmetry and density. Only 1475115 (three rings) and 1733538 (nested hexagons) actually present 'one boundary inside another'; the rest are a single boundary around a tangle. And 'gold and umber' is one gold hue modulated by stroke alpha - I recorded no second tone before reading the brief.
composition: Split. Where a bright continuous container reads against a ghosted core there is a real focal hierarchy: 1243682 has a genuine focus (the eye, a concentric circle with a pupil, at the base of the diamond), 1283437 has its mask over a pendant ring, 1733538 has a clean nested-hexagon read. But 1203347, 1561509 and 1310661 are even fields of incident with nothing dominant, and 1561509's core fills its circle edge to edge - the opposite of the 'small dense centre held at the middle' the brief specifies. In the other direction 1985692 (two tiny marks in a small square inside a large empty ring) and 1475115 (a pea-sized knot inside three rings) under-use the frame so badly they read unfinished rather than restrained. The frame is used well in the neutral row with a generous dark margin; it is abandoned in stress, where 1203347, 1243682 and 1283437 all run into the edges.
collectionCoherence: The strongest axis. All twelve share one hairline stroke weight, one gold-on-ink palette, one centred container-plus-core structure and one drafting idiom, so the sheet reads unmistakably as a single project. The two most distant members - 1366079, a mirrored crowned totem in a hexagon, and 1991107, an asymmetric scatter in a diamond - are still obviously siblings. Nothing here reads as a folder of unrelated files; if the brief had been met on the other axes this one would carry the collection.
palette: Chosen, consistent, and narrow. A single brass/ochre hue over a near-black blue-tinted ink, with the ground supporting rather than competing - the dark genuinely holds 1733538, 1446330 and 1985692. But the only tonal instrument is stroke opacity, and it stops working at browse size: on 1475115 and 1985692 the ghosted strokes drop out entirely at 120px so the 'contrast range' becomes plain absence, and in 1561509 and 1310661 neutral the mid-alpha overlaps sum into a flat wash instead of reading as depth. Against a brief asking for gold AND umber over deep ink, I saw gold over deep ink and no umber.
seedVariation: Correctly pitched overall - these are twelve works, not one work at twelve rotations. Container silhouette, symmetry order and density all move independently, and 1985692 and 1561509 sit at genuine opposite extremes of density. The failures are local and in the collapsing direction, not the fracturing one: 1733538 and 1446330 are near-duplicates at browse size (hexagon plus small central core, differing mainly in whether the core is a rosette or a pair of blobs), and 1203347 and 1991107 both resolve to an unstructured scatter of squares and circles with no distinguishing structure. Nothing is so far out that the project stops being one project.
thumbnailSurvival: Good on the work's own terms, and that is the irony. At 120px the container silhouettes cleanly sort the twelve - circle, hexagon, square, diamond are all legible - and the face reads hold: 1243682's eye and 1283437's pendant ring both survive. Density still separates 1561509 from 1733538. The weak tiles are 1985692, which reads as an empty ring and looks like a failed render, 1475115, which reads as rings around a smudge, and the 1733538/1446330 pair which merge. But the single thing that survives BEST at 120 is the state change - the row the brief wanted a casual viewer not to notice is the row you notice first.
marketResponse: Highly visible, cleanly built, and the wrong change. This is not 'a slight tightening or loosening of the enclosure'; it is rupture and reconstitution. 1203347 neutral to stress loses the enclosure altogether; 1310661 stress shrinks and rotates inside a newly-appeared square with four loose diamonds at the corners; 1283437 stress grows past three frame edges and its circle becomes a shield; 1243682's boundary changes from circle to diamond. Recovery is a real third state rather than a copy of neutral - 1310661 recovery is denser than its own neutral with more hexagonal rosettes, 1203347 recovery carries noticeably larger circles - so the arc intact/ruptured/repaired is delivered legibly. Delivered, well made, and precisely contrary to the commission.
tokenIdentity: Holds in three of four sampled tokens and breaks in the fourth. 1243682 keeps its eye and its crown of fanned squares in all three states; 1283437 keeps its mask silhouette and the pendant ring below it; 1310661 keeps its hexagonal rosettes and can be matched across the row. 1203347 is the break: in stress the outer circle is gone and the object is a drift of tumbling squares off the top-left corner, and without the caption I could not have matched it to its own neutral. Under a brief that promised the enclosure merely tightens or loosens, a token that loses its enclosure has been replaced rather than affected.
artifacts: Frame clipping in the stress row on 1203347 (elements exiting the top-left corner), 1243682 (crown touching both side margins) and 1283437 (crossing the top and both sides) - which also directly contradicts 'most of the frame given to the dark'. 1561509 carries two small circles at the bottom of the head form that read as accidental feet or castors rather than as drawn elements. Interior mush at full 256px size in 1561509, and in the neutral frames of 1310661 and 1283437, where overlapping mid-alpha polygons sum to an undifferentiated field. 1985692 is sparse enough to read as an incomplete render rather than a quiet one. I found no vanished strokes, no half-cut shapes and no viewBox truncation anywhere in the neutral row.
reasoning: The gate decides this and nothing else needed to. The brief commissioned a still, settled object that has already finished happening, whose response to the market is faint enough that a casual viewer would not notice it at thumbnail size, with an explicit instruction not to manufacture drama. Before I had read a word of that, I described a work whose defining feature is a violent, edge-clipping, container-destroying stress state that is the most conspicuous thing on the 120px sheet - and whose seed-to-seed variation runs on container shape rather than on the number of enclosures the brief nominated. Three of the brief's four sentences are contradicted by the pictures: the enclosure structure is mostly single rather than concentric, the palette is gold without umber, and the market response is drama rather than a faint tightening. The work is not incompetent - collection coherence is genuinely strong, the state machine is well built, 1243682 and 1283437 are handsome objects - but it is a good answer to a different brief, one asking for a sigil that shatters and reforms under drawdown. Under the rule I was given, that is REFUSE however accomplished it is.
wouldChange: Cut the amplitude of the state response by roughly an order of magnitude and move it from structure to boundary. Stress should change only the spacing and stroke weight of the enclosures - rings drawing a few percent inward, hairlines thickening slightly - with the element set, the container silhouette and the composition all held fixed, so 1203347 keeps its circle and 1283437 never leaves its margin; no element should ever cross the frame edge in any state. Then make the seed axis the one the brief named: vary the COUNT of concentric boundaries from one to five (1475115 and 1733538 are the only two currently doing this and should be the model) and vary the character of the held centre, rather than swapping circle for hexagon for square for diamond. Introduce the missing umber as a true second pigment for the outer enclosures against gold for the centre, instead of relying on alpha, which vanishes at 120px on 1475115 and 1985692. Finally raise the floor on the empty tiles - 1985692 needs a centre with enough incident to read as held rather than absent - and pull 1733538 and 1446330 apart so they are not the same thumbnail twice.
